issues.title: [P0][security] Never send xAI session credentials to custom model-catalog endpoints
issues.body:
## Summary

A custom `/models` endpoint can currently receive the user's xAI session token.

`ListModelsEndpoint::from_endpoints` classifies a configured custom models endpoint as API-key authenticated. In `fetch_models_blocking`, the API-key branch first reads `XAI_API_KEY`, then falls back to `auth.key`. When the user is signed in to xAI and configures a third-party or local catalog without `XAI_API_KEY`, that fallback is the xAI session credential and is sent as `Authorization: Bearer ...` to the custom host.

This crosses the first-party credential boundary and must fail closed.

## Evidence / affected code

- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/remote/client.rs`
  - `EndpointAuth`
  - `ListModelsEndpoint::from_endpoints`
  - `fetch_models_blocking`
- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/agent/models.rs`
  - `ModelFetchAuth::resolve`
- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/11-custom-models.md`

## Required behavior

1. Credentials obtained from xAI session/OAuth login must never be attached to a non-xAI catalog endpoint.
2. The custom-catalog path must not use `auth.key` as a fallback for a missing external credential.
3. Missing custom-catalog credentials must produce a clear, redacted configuration error, unless anonymous catalog access is explicitly configured.
4. Official xAI model discovery must continue to support first-party session authentication.
5. Redirects must not allow a first-party request to carry credentials to a different origin.

## Implementation plan

1. Split first-party session auth from custom-catalog auth in `ListModelsEndpoint`.
2. Add a single endpoint/origin classification helper that decides whether first-party session credentials are permitted.
3. Remove the `auth.key` fallback from every custom endpoint credential path.
4. For the minimal security patch, require an explicitly resolved credential for the custom endpoint, or explicit anonymous access; otherwise return `BackendError::Auth` before constructing/sending the request.
5. Ensure first-party identity headers (`X-XAI-Token-Auth`, user/deployment identity, and equivalent session headers) are absent on custom origins.
6. Disable redirects for catalog discovery, or install a redirect policy that re-validates the destination origin and strips credentials before following.
7. Update the custom-model guide so it never implies that xAI login authenticates a third-party catalog.

The broader configurable catalog-auth feature is tracked separately. This issue is the fail-closed security patch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Custom endpoint + xAI session + no external key sends no request containing the xAI session token.
- [ ] The error identifies the missing custom-endpoint credential without printing any secret fragment.
- [ ] Custom endpoint + explicit external Bearer key sends only that key.
- [ ] Official xAI discovery still receives the expected first-party session authentication.
- [ ] A cross-origin redirect cannot receive first-party credentials.
- [ ] No test uses real network access or real credentials.

## Tests

Add mock-server tests around `fetch_models_blocking` for:

1. custom endpoint, session credential present, external key absent;
2. custom endpoint, explicit external key present;
3. official endpoint with session auth;
4. custom endpoint returning a redirect to another origin;
5. error/log output containing sentinel secrets, asserting the sentinel never appears.

Run at minimum:

```bash
cargo test -p xai-grok-shell remote::
cargo test -p xai-grok-shell agent::models::
```

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not silently retry with another credential class.
- Do not store or migrate secrets in this patch.
- Do not broaden the hosts allowed to receive session credentials.
- Do not implement the full provider onboarding flow here.

issues.title: [P0][security] Remove credential fragments from logs and telemetry
issues.body:
## Summary

Multiple code paths log prefixes or suffixes of live credentials. Examples include:

- the first 20 characters of `Authorization`;
- the first 12 characters of `x-api-key`;
- subagent and parent `key_prefix` values;
- access-token and refresh-token suffixes during agent initialization and disk refresh.

Partial credentials are still sensitive. They can aid correlation, reduce brute-force space, leak provider/account structure, and become a complete secret when combined with another log source. INFO-level logs are especially risky because they may be collected by terminal logs, CI, support bundles, external OpenTelemetry backends, or crash reports.

## Evidence / affected code

- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-sampler/src/client.rs`
  - request-header INFO logging in `post`
- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/agent/subagent/handle_request.rs`
  - `subagent spawn credentials`
- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/agent/mvp_agent/acp_agent.rs`
  - auth initialization and disk-refresh telemetry
- Any shared helper such as `token_suffix` or `key_prefix` when used in logs/telemetry

## Required behavior

1. No production log, telemetry event, error, panic, or support export may contain any substring of a credential.
2. Diagnostics may record non-secret facts such as `credential_present`, `auth_scheme`, `credential_source`, or a process-local opaque correlation ID.
3. A correlation identifier, if truly needed, must be one-way, keyed/process-local, truncated, and documented as non-stable across runs. Prefer no identifier.
4. Redaction must occur before data reaches tracing fields, unified logs, OpenTelemetry, or error formatting.

## Implementation plan

1. Inventory every logging/telemetry call that receives:
   - `Authorization`;
   - `x-api-key`;
   - access tokens;
   - refresh tokens;
   - deployment keys;
   - provider API keys;
   - values returned by `token_suffix`/`key_prefix`.
2. Replace raw fragments with structured booleans and enums:
   - `authorization_present`;
   - `x_api_key_present`;
   - `auth_scheme`;
   - `credential_source`;
   - `same_credential_source` where comparison is required.
3. Introduce a small secret-safe diagnostic type or helper so a secret cannot accidentally implement useful `Display`/`Debug` output.
4. Remove or deprecate token-fragment helpers from logging call sites.
5. Ensure debug mode and sampling logs follow the same rule; debug must not weaken the boundary.
6. Add a repository-wide regression test/helper that captures logs while sentinel secrets flow through all known paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No credential prefix/suffix is logged at INFO, DEBUG, WARN, ERROR, unified log, sampling log, or OpenTelemetry.
- [ ] Existing operational diagnostics still show auth scheme/source and whether a credential is present.
- [ ] Sentinel access, refresh, deployment, Bearer, and `x-api-key` values never appear in captured logs.
- [ ] Error messages returned to the TUI/CLI are also secret-safe.
- [ ] Documentation no longer recommends logging key fragments for diagnosis.

## Tests

Add log-capture tests covering:

- sampler request construction for Bearer and `x-api-key`;
- subagent spawn with different parent/child credentials;
- auth initialization before and after disk reload;
- failed provider requests;
- `--debug`, sampling logs, and unified telemetry layers where test seams exist.

Use unique sentinel strings and assert both the full value and every significant prefix/suffix are absent.

```bash
cargo test -p xai-grok-sampler
cargo test -p xai-grok-shell auth
cargo test -p xai-grok-shell subagent
```

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not merely shorten the fragment.
- Do not hide the issue behind a lower log level.
- Do not hash secrets with an unkeyed stable hash.
- Do not remove useful non-secret auth diagnostics.

issues.title: [P1][privacy] Apply the first-party metadata boundary to all non-xAI requests
issues.body:
## Summary

Non-xAI inference endpoints are protected from some first-party identity headers, but they can still receive internal Grok metadata such as conversation ID, request ID, session ID, agent ID, model override, client identifier, and distributed tracing context.

These values are not required by OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible providers and create unnecessary cross-provider correlation. A local or third-party provider should receive only protocol-required headers, the configured provider credential, explicitly configured extra headers, and a minimal user agent unless the user opts into additional diagnostics.

## Evidence / affected code

- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-sampler/src/client.rs`
  - `GrokRequestHeaders::apply`
  - request construction and post-injector scrubbing
- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-sampler/src/config.rs`
  - `client_identifier`, origin identity, and header injector
- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/session/acp_session_impl/sampler_turn.rs`
  - trace-context injector installation
- Endpoint classification shared with model-catalog discovery

## Required behavior

For a non-xAI origin, default request headers must exclude:

- xAI session/conversation/agent identifiers;
- xAI user/deployment identity;
- internal model-override headers;
- first-party client identifiers;
- `traceparent`/`tracestate` that link the request to first-party telemetry.

The request may include:

- protocol headers such as `Content-Type` and `Accept`;
- the provider's selected auth header;
- a generic, non-identifying User-Agent;
- explicitly configured provider headers after validation.

## Implementation plan

1. Define an explicit `EndpointTrustClass` (for example `FirstPartyXai`, `External`, `Local`) at config resolution time.
2. Pass that classification into request construction rather than re-deriving it independently in several crates.
3. Replace the current partial identity stripping with an allowlist for `External`/`Local` requests.
4. Apply the boundary after all header injectors so a trace or custom injector cannot re-add blocked first-party metadata.
5. Add an opt-in provider setting such as `send_internal_diagnostics = true` only if a real use case exists. It must never permit xAI session credentials.
6. Surface the effective metadata policy in `grok inspect --json` and provider doctor output.
7. Document which headers are sent to each trust class.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A captured external/local request contains none of the blocked first-party identifiers by default.
- [ ] Official xAI requests retain required first-party headers.
- [ ] Header injectors cannot re-add blocked metadata to external/local requests.
- [ ] Provider-configured headers still work unless their names are explicitly forbidden for security reasons.
- [ ] The policy is deterministic and covered for all supported API backends.
- [ ] `grok inspect --json` can show the trust class and metadata policy without exposing secrets.

## Tests

Build table-driven mock-server tests for:

- first-party xAI endpoint;
- external HTTPS endpoint;
- loopback/local endpoint;
- OpenAI Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic-compatible backends;
- custom header injector attempting to add `traceparent` and `x-grok-session-id`;
- configured safe extra headers.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not use a fragile substring check for host classification.
- Do not remove protocol-required provider headers.
- Do not make privacy depend on debug/release build mode.
- Do not classify arbitrary reverse proxies as first-party without explicit, safe configuration.

issues.title: [P0][security] Fail closed for unclassified MCP/custom tools in restricted subagent modes
issues.body:
## Summary

Restricted subagent capability modes currently preserve tools whose `ToolConfig.kind` is `None`. The code explicitly notes that MCP/custom tools created through `ToolConfig::from_id()` can be unclassified and are retained unconditionally.

This means a `ReadOnly`, `ReadWrite`, or `Execute` subagent can still receive an unclassified MCP/custom tool whose real behavior writes files, executes commands, sends network requests, or mutates external systems. The named capability mode therefore does not form a reliable permission boundary.

## Evidence / affected code

- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-tools/src/implementations/grok_build/task/types.rs`
  - `SubagentCapabilityModeExt::filter_tool_config`
  - the `None => true` branch
  - MCP/custom tools created without `ToolKind`
- MCP/custom tool registration paths that construct `ToolConfig`
- Role/persona/subagent configuration that selects a restricted capability mode

## Required behavior

1. Restricted modes must fail closed for tools that cannot be classified.
2. Every MCP/custom tool exposed to a restricted subagent must have explicit capability metadata.
3. `ReadOnly` must not receive tools that can write, execute, mutate external state, or invoke an unclassified nested capability.
4. `All` may preserve unclassified tools only as an explicitly unrestricted mode.
5. Existing safe MCP tools need a migration path, not a blanket compatibility exception.

## Implementation plan

1. Add a capability descriptor for external tools. A single `ToolKind` may be insufficient; support a set of effects such as:
   - read local;
   - write local;
   - execute;
   - network read;
   - external mutation;
   - secret access;
   - subagent spawn.
2. Require MCP/custom registrations to provide the descriptor, derive it from trusted manifest metadata, or be marked `Unclassified`.
3. Change restricted-mode filtering so `Unclassified` is excluded by default.
4. Add an explicit configuration allowlist for users who intentionally permit a named unclassified tool in a restricted role. Emit a warning and show it in `grok inspect`.
5. Ensure tool aliases/wrappers inherit the underlying capability descriptor.
6. Re-run orphan background-task pruning after capability filtering.
7. Add diagnostics explaining why a tool was removed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fake unclassified MCP tool is absent from every restricted capability mode.
- [ ] A classified read-only MCP tool remains available in `ReadOnly`.
- [ ] Write/execute/external-mutation tools are absent from `ReadOnly`.
- [ ] `All` retains the complete toolset.
- [ ] Explicit per-tool overrides are visible in inspection output and tested.
- [ ] Nested/wrapped tools cannot bypass classification.

## Tests

Add table-driven tests covering built-in, MCP, custom, alias, and wrapped tools for each capability mode. Include a malicious fake tool with `kind = None` and mutation semantics.

```bash
cargo test -p xai-grok-tools subagent
cargo test -p xai-grok-shell subagent
```

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not infer safety from a tool name.
- Do not keep `None => true` for compatibility.
- Do not silently promote an unknown tool to read-only.
- Do not change top-level user permissions without an explicit migration note.

issues.title: [P1][security] Harden `grok agent serve` secrets and non-loopback exposure
issues.body:
## Summary

`grok agent serve` generates a 12-character secret from the beginning of a UUID-derived hexadecimal string, prints the secret, and prints a plaintext `ws://` URL containing the secret in the query string.

The default bind address is loopback, but users can select a non-loopback address. In that case the current defaults create a weak remote-exposure posture: limited secret entropy, plaintext transport, and a credential in a URL that can be copied into shell history, proxy logs, terminal logs, or screenshots.

## Evidence / affected code

- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/src/app/cli.rs`
  - `ServeArgs`
  - `ServeArgs::get_secret`
  - `generate_random_key`
- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager-bin/src/main.rs`
  - `print_serve_startup_info`
  - serve-mode startup and WebSocket authentication

## Required behavior

1. Loopback usage should remain easy.
2. Generated secrets must use a cryptographically secure RNG and at least 128 bits of entropy.
3. Binding to a non-loopback address must require an explicit acknowledgement and a secure authentication/transport plan.
4. Secrets should not be embedded in URLs or printed into non-interactive logs by default.
5. Authentication comparison must be constant-time where practical.

## Implementation plan

1. Replace UUID substring generation with `rand::rngs::OsRng` and a URL-safe 32-byte token.
2. Add a bind-address preflight:
   - loopback: allow generated secret;
   - non-loopback: require explicit `--allow-remote` plus an explicit secret, or a documented TLS/tunnel mode.
3. Prefer an `Authorization` header or a one-time handshake over `server-key` query parameters. Keep a time-limited compatibility path if existing clients require the query form.
4. Print only:
   - address;
   - whether authentication is enabled;
   - instructions for retrieving/copying the secret interactively.
   Avoid printing the secret when stderr is not a TTY.
5. Warn or reject plaintext `ws://` on non-loopback interfaces.
6. Add secret redaction to errors, access logs, and tracing.
7. Document safe SSH tunnel and reverse-proxy examples.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generated tokens provide at least 128 bits of entropy and are tested for length/format.
- [ ] Non-loopback bind without an explicit remote-exposure acknowledgement fails before listening.
- [ ] Non-loopback plaintext exposure is rejected or clearly gated.
- [ ] Default logs and URLs do not contain the secret.
- [ ] Existing loopback clients have a documented migration path.
- [ ] Authentication failure behavior does not reveal token prefixes or timing-sensitive details.

## Tests

- Unit-test token generation and bind classification.
- Integration-test loopback startup.
- Integration-test rejection of `0.0.0.0`/public bind without the required flags.
- Capture output and assert sentinel secrets are absent.
- Test legacy query authentication only if retained.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not claim query-string credentials are safe because the service is usually local.
- Do not weaken loopback authentication.
- Do not silently expose a server when validation fails.

issues.title: [P1][bug] Fail closed when a model requires an unavailable agent harness
issues.body:
## Summary

A zero-turn model switch can continue with the previous agent harness when the newly selected model requires a different harness but the required `AgentDefinition` cannot be found.

The code warns and proceeds. This produces a model/harness combination the catalog says is incompatible: wrong system prompt, wrong toolset, or wrong protocol assumptions. After turns have already run, the same mismatch is rejected, so behavior is inconsistent.

## Evidence / affected code

- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/agent/handlers/model_switch.rs`
  - harness compatibility validation
  - zero-turn rebuild path
  - warning path when the required agent definition is missing
- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/session/acp_session_impl/model_switch.rs`
  - session-level model/harness application

## Expected behavior

A model switch must be atomic. Before mutating the session, resolve and validate:

- catalog model;
- readiness/auth;
- API backend;
- required harness/agent definition;
- toolset;
- context-window/compaction settings.

If any prerequisite is unavailable, reject the switch and preserve the complete previous state.

## Implementation plan

1. Introduce a `PreparedModelSwitch` value containing every resolved prerequisite.
2. Resolve the required agent definition before changing model state, chat state, auth, prompt, persistence, or UI-visible selection.
3. Return a structured error such as `RequiredHarnessUnavailable { model_id, agent_type }`.
4. Let the TUI offer a new-session flow only when that flow can actually resolve the harness.
5. Emit the `"model changed"` event only after commit succeeds; emit a separate failure event otherwise.
6. Ensure the same validation path is used for:
   - `/model`;
   - default model changes;
   - ACP `set_session_model`;
   - restored sessions;
   - subagent explicit model overrides where applicable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missing required harness leaves model, prompt, toolset, auth, compaction, and persistence unchanged.
- [ ] No success telemetry is emitted for a rejected switch.
- [ ] Zero-turn and non-zero-turn sessions follow consistent compatibility rules.
- [ ] A valid required harness still rebuilds successfully.
- [ ] The user-facing error names the model/harness but contains no credential/config secret.

## Tests

Add state-snapshot tests for:

1. zero-turn switch with missing required harness;
2. zero-turn switch with valid required harness;
3. non-zero-turn incompatible switch;
4. switch through TUI/default-model/ACP paths;
5. event ordering: failure must not emit `"model changed"`.

```bash
cargo test -p xai-grok-shell model_switch
cargo test -p xai-grok-pager switch_model
```

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not silently reuse the old harness.
- Do not partially apply the new model before validation completes.
- Do not solve automatic harness installation in this issue.

issues.title: [P1][bug] Resolve compaction and context settings by catalog ID, not wire slug
issues.body:
## Summary

The fork intentionally separates the catalog key from the provider wire slug so two configured models may share the same wire model name. The model-switch path still derives the new auto-compaction threshold by looking up `model_sampling.model`, which is the wire slug.

With duplicate slugs, the lookup can select the wrong catalog entry and apply the wrong context window, compaction threshold, or related model metadata.

## Evidence / affected code

- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/agent/handlers/model_switch.rs`
  - `new_auto_compact_threshold_percent`
  - lookup by `model_sampling.model`
- Catalog/model resolution helpers such as `find_model_by_id`
- Any persistence or restoration path that stores only the wire slug

## Expected behavior

- Catalog identity is authoritative for configuration and persistence.
- Wire slug is used only in the outbound provider payload.
- Duplicate wire slugs must remain fully independent.

## Implementation plan

1. Carry the selected catalog ID and resolved `ModelEntry` through `PreparedModelSwitch`.
2. Read context window, compaction threshold, API backend, auth scheme, and capabilities directly from that resolved entry.
3. Audit every model-switch/restoration path for accidental lookup by wire slug.
4. Persist both:
   - catalog ID (authoritative local identity);
   - wire slug (diagnostic/provider payload).
5. Add a migration/fallback for older sessions that persisted only a slug:
   - resolve only when unambiguous;
   - otherwise require explicit user selection rather than choosing the first match.
6. Make diagnostic output show both values when they differ.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two catalog entries with the same wire slug can have different context windows and compaction settings.
- [ ] Switching between them applies the selected entry's metadata every time.
- [ ] Session restore preserves the selected catalog entry.
- [ ] Legacy ambiguous slug-only sessions fail with an actionable choice instead of silently selecting one.
- [ ] Outbound requests still use the configured wire slug.

## Tests

Create fixtures with:

- `local-fast` and `remote-accurate`;
- both using wire model `qwen`;
- different base URLs, context windows, and compaction percentages.

Cover new session, switch, restart/restore, subagent, and legacy slug-only migration.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not prohibit duplicate wire slugs.
- Do not use display name as identity.
- Do not silently rewrite the user's catalog keys.

issues.title: [P1][bug] Persist the default model only after a successful switch
[P1][providers] Support explicit auth schemes for custom model-catalog discovery
issues.body:
## Summary

Custom inference models support multiple auth schemes (`bearer`, `x_api_key`, and `none`), but custom model-catalog discovery is effectively hard-coded to Bearer authentication and `XAI_API_KEY`.

This breaks common setups:

- local OpenAI-compatible servers with no auth;
- Anthropic-style gateways using `x-api-key`;
- providers with a dedicated catalog key/env variable;
- model registries requiring additional safe headers.

This issue follows the P0 fail-closed credential-boundary fix and adds an explicit, provider-owned catalog auth configuration.

## Proposed configuration

Use names that clearly separate catalog discovery from inference, for example:

```toml
[models]
endpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/models"
catalog_auth_scheme = "none" # none | bearer | x_api_key
catalog_env_key = "LM_STUDIO_API_KEY"
catalog_headers = { "X-Organization" = "..." }
```

Exact field names may change, but they must not overload per-model inference credentials.

## Implementation plan

1. Add a typed `CatalogAuthConfig` with:
   - auth scheme;
   - ordered env-key candidates;
   - safe extra headers;
   - optional timeout and redirect policy.
2. Parse it with the same fail-closed unknown/invalid-value behavior as model auth.
3. Resolve credentials from the configured environment key only; never fall back to xAI session credentials.
4. Implement request application for:
   - no auth;
   - `Authorization: Bearer`;
   - `x-api-key`.
5. Validate header names and prevent configured headers from overriding protected auth/identity headers.
6. Decide whether catalog responses can describe per-model metadata (`api`, context window, capabilities, auth scheme). Treat remote metadata as untrusted and validate every field.
7. Expose the resolved scheme and credential source name—not value—in inspection/doctor output.
8. Update docs with complete examples for local, OpenAI-compatible, and Anthropic-compatible catalogs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Anonymous local catalog works without a fake key.
- [ ] Bearer and `x-api-key` catalog auth use the configured environment variable.
- [ ] xAI session tokens are impossible on custom catalog requests.
- [ ] Invalid auth schemes fail closed with a path-specific config error.
- [ ] Extra headers cannot override protected headers.
- [ ] Catalog and inference auth can differ.
- [ ] All output is secret-redacted.

## Tests

Use mock servers to assert exact headers for each scheme and to cover:

- missing env var;
- empty/whitespace env var name;
- invalid scheme;
- redirect;
- protected-header override;
- catalog response with valid/invalid optional metadata;
- backward-compatible configuration without the new fields.

## Dependencies

- Complete `[P0][security] Never send xAI session credentials to custom model-catalog endpoints` first.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not store literal API keys in generated TOML by default.
- Do not infer auth scheme from the hostname.
- Do not trust arbitrary catalog-provided headers or credentials.

issues.title: [P2][config] Normalize and reject whitespace-only `env_key` entries
issues.body:
## Summary

`EnvKeys::new` filters empty strings but does not trim entries. A value such as `"   "` is retained and can become the primary environment-variable name.

The resulting readiness error is confusing, and downstream code may attempt to resolve an environment variable whose name is only whitespace. Duplicate keys with surrounding whitespace are also not normalized.

## Affected code

- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/agent/config.rs`
  - `EnvKeys::new`
  - `EnvKeys::primary`
  - credential/readiness diagnostics
- custom-model configuration parsing and documentation

## Implementation plan

1. Trim every configured env-key candidate.
2. Remove entries that are empty after trimming.
3. Deduplicate while preserving first occurrence/order.
4. Validate environment-variable names with a conservative cross-platform rule, or at minimum reject control characters, `=`, and whitespace.
5. Return a path-specific config warning/error for invalid entries instead of silently selecting them.
6. Ensure diagnostics show the normalized variable name only, never its value.
7. Update examples to use valid uppercase names.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `"   "` is not accepted as a credential source.
- [ ] `" API_KEY "` normalizes to `API_KEY`.
- [ ] Duplicate normalized entries appear once.
- [ ] Invalid names produce a clear error pointing to the model/config field.
- [ ] Existing valid configurations preserve precedence.

## Tests

Add unit tests for:

- empty and whitespace-only input;
- surrounding whitespace;
- duplicates;
- `=` and control characters;
- multiple valid fallback keys;
- serialization/diagnostics.

```bash
cargo test -p xai-grok-shell env_keys
```

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not read or print environment-variable values.
- Do not reorder distinct valid candidates.
- Keep the change narrowly scoped.

issues.title: [P1][subagents] Refresh MCP, skills, and tool capabilities at child spawn time
issues.body:
## Summary

Several subagent inputs are snapshots captured when the parent session actor is created, including MCP configuration/pool state, tool schema, and skills. MCP servers added later, plugin reloads, and skill reloads may therefore be missing from a child spawned during a long-running session.

This creates capability drift: the parent can use a newly loaded tool or skill, but a later child receives stale capabilities and fails unpredictably.

## Evidence / affected code

- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/agent/subagent/mod.rs`
  - `parent_mcp_configs`
  - `parent_mcp_pool`
  - `parent_tool_snapshot`
  - `parent_skills`
  - comments describing spawn-time snapshots
- `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/agent/subagent/handle_request.rs`
- session commands for MCP/plugin/skill reload

## Expected behavior

Each subagent spawn must resolve a consistent, current capability snapshot from the parent immediately before child construction. It must still honor trust, permission, capability-mode, and isolation filtering.

## Implementation plan

1. Add a parent-session actor query returning a versioned `SubagentCapabilitySnapshot` containing:
   - active MCP definitions and connection handles/references;
   - current tool schema and capability metadata;
   - current skills;
   - trust/permission generation;
   - plugin/config generation.
2. Request this snapshot at child spawn time rather than storing long-lived copies in the coordinator.
3. Keep the snapshot immutable for that child after spawn so its tool contract does not mutate mid-turn.
4. If the parent changes while the snapshot is being built, retry or use an atomic generation check.
5. Apply restricted capability filtering after the live snapshot is obtained.
6. Return an actionable error if refresh fails; do not silently fall back to stale state.
7. Record non-secret snapshot generations in diagnostics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A server/skill/plugin loaded after parent session creation is available to a subsequently spawned child.
- [ ] A removed or disabled capability is not inherited by a subsequently spawned child.
- [ ] Existing children keep their immutable spawn snapshot.
- [ ] Trust and permission restrictions are re-evaluated at spawn time.
- [ ] Refresh failure is visible and does not silently use stale data.
- [ ] No child receives a broader capability set than the parent permits.

## Tests

Cover:

1. parent starts, then MCP is added, then child spawns;
2. skill reload before child spawn;
3. plugin removal/disable before child spawn;
4. concurrent reload and spawn using generation checks;
5. restricted capability mode over the refreshed snapshot;
6. parent session actor unavailable.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not share mutable tool registries directly with children.
- Do not skip trust checks for performance.
- Do not reconnect every MCP server unnecessarily; reuse safe live handles where supported.

issues.title: [P1][UX] Add provider diagnostics to `/doctor` and `grok doctor --json`
[P1][UX] Add safe interactive provider onboarding and config editing
issues.body:
## Summary

Adding a custom provider currently requires manual TOML editing, knowledge of catalog IDs versus wire slugs, API backend selection, auth scheme, context window, and environment-variable precedence.

Add an interactive onboarding flow that produces valid, reviewable configuration and immediately runs provider diagnostics.

## Proposed flows

CLI:

```bash
grok models add
grok models edit <catalog-id>
grok models remove <catalog-id>
```

TUI:

- `/model add`
- an “Add provider/model” action in the picker
- “Diagnose” and “Edit config” actions for unready entries

## Required inputs

- provider preset or custom;
- catalog ID;
- wire model slug;
- base URL;
- API backend;
- auth scheme;
- credential environment-variable name;
- context window;
- optional capabilities/reasoning efforts;
- optional model-catalog endpoint/auth;
- role/default assignment.

## Implementation plan

1. Define a typed editable model/provider configuration independent of UI.
2. Add presets for common compatible shapes, but always show the generated fields before writing.
3. Never request or store the secret value by default. Ask the user to set a named environment variable; optionally integrate an existing secret store in a separate explicit flow.
4. Validate URLs and reject embedded credentials.
5. Preserve comments/order in `config.toml` using `toml_edit`.
6. Write atomically with backup/rollback on failure.
7. Run offline diagnostics before commit and optional live diagnostics after confirmation.
8. Detect catalog ID collisions and duplicate wire slugs, explaining the distinction.
9. Show an exact diff and require confirmation before writing.
10. Hot-reload the catalog and verify the new entry appears with the expected readiness state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can add anonymous local, Bearer, and `x-api-key` models without hand-editing TOML.
- [ ] Generated config parses and round-trips without losing unrelated comments/settings.
- [ ] Secrets are not written to TOML or printed.
- [ ] Invalid URL/backend/auth combinations are blocked before write.
- [ ] Cancel/failure leaves the original file byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [ ] Duplicate catalog IDs are rejected; duplicate wire slugs are allowed with clear UX.
- [ ] The new model is hot-reloaded and diagnosable.

## Tests

- Golden tests for generated TOML.
- Round-trip/comment-preservation tests.
- Atomic write/rollback and concurrent edit tests.
- Wizard state-machine tests for each auth/backend.
- Live mock-provider validation.
- Secret-redaction snapshots.

## Dependencies

- Provider auth-boundary fix.
- Explicit catalog auth configuration.
- Provider doctor engine.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not write raw API keys to config by default.
- Do not overwrite unrelated user settings.
- Do not silently guess context window or capabilities; mark unknown values explicitly.

issues.title: [P1][UX] Make the model picker provider-aware and actionable
[P1][resilience] Add ordered model/provider failover without widening permissions
issues.body:
## Summary

Long-running work is vulnerable to provider quota exhaustion, rate limits, outages, and transient protocol failures. Add explicit ordered failover chains for primary, auxiliary, and subagent roles.

Failover must preserve security and correctness. It must not replay side-effecting work after partial output, cross credential boundaries, switch to an incompatible harness, or silently degrade required capabilities.

## Proposed configuration

Example only:

```toml
[fallbacks]
default = ["grok-primary", "local-qwen"]
web_search = ["grok-search", "external-search"]
verifier = ["strong-verifier", "local-verifier"]
```

Each entry references a catalog ID, not a wire slug.

## Failure classes

Define which failures are eligible:

- pre-output connection/DNS/TLS timeout;
- 429/quota exhausted after configured retry threshold;
- retryable 5xx;
- provider-declared temporary unavailable.

Do not automatically fail over after:

- any tool side effect;
- user-visible partial model output unless explicitly supported;
- authentication/config errors that require user correction;
- safety/policy rejection;
- incompatible required capability/harness.

## Implementation plan

1. Add typed failover policy and failure classification.
2. Pre-validate every candidate for readiness, trust class, required capabilities, harness, context size, and permission/tool compatibility.
3. Freeze the request input and side-effect state before first attempt.
4. Permit automatic fallback only before output/tool execution.
5. Record attempt history and selected fallback in session/workflow state.
6. Show a concise notice with reason; do not hide the provider switch.
7. Add per-role chains and optional maximum attempts/cooldown.
8. Integrate with workflow checkpoint/resume so a later phase can use a fallback safely.
9. Ensure credentials are resolved independently per candidate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A retryable pre-output outage can move to the next compatible configured catalog ID.
- [ ] Partial output or a tool side effect prevents silent replay.
- [ ] Failover never forwards one provider's credential to another.
- [ ] A candidate missing required tools/vision/context/harness is skipped with a recorded reason.
- [ ] The user can disable failover globally or per role.
- [ ] Attempt history is visible in TUI/JSON diagnostics.
- [ ] Deterministic tests do not contact real providers.

## Tests

Use scripted mock providers for:

- connect timeout then success;
- 429 then fallback;
- retryable 5xx;
- 401/config error (no fallback unless policy explicitly says otherwise);
- partial SSE output then failure;
- tool call emitted then failure;
- incompatible context/capability/harness;
- distinct Bearer and `x-api-key` credentials.

## Dependencies

- Provider credential and metadata boundaries.
- Catalog-ID correctness.
- Capability-aware model metadata.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not retry side effects.
- Do not choose an unconfigured model.
- Do not silently reduce permissions or required capabilities.
- Do not implement benchmark-based routing in this issue.

issues.title: [P1][routing] Add capability-aware subagent model routing and loss reports
[P1][workflow] Persist checkpoints and resume interrupted workflow runs
[P1][resume] Add portable cross-agent handoff bundles separate from session restore
issues.body:
## Summary

`/resume` currently restores a Grok session and `/export` produces a Markdown transcript. Neither provides a compact, portable handoff that can be imported into a fresh agent/session/model without replaying the full history.

Add a versioned handoff bundle designed for cross-agent continuation.

## Required distinction

- **Session restore**: reopen the original persisted conversation/runtime state.
- **Workflow resume**: continue a durable workflow checkpoint.
- **Handoff import**: create a fresh session from a minimal, explicit transfer package.

These must remain separate commands and data formats.

## Bundle contents

Required fields:

- objective and current success criteria;
- user constraints and non-goals;
- decisions and rationale;
- current plan/status;
- remaining tasks in dependency order;
- changed files, commits, branches/worktrees;
- tests run and results;
- known failures/blockers;
- model/tool/capability requirements;
- relevant references/paths;
- source session/run metadata;
- schema version.

Optional attachments:

- selected diffs/patches;
- compacted evidence excerpts;
- structured task output.

Exclude by default:

- full transcript;
- credentials/environment values;
- unrelated personal/session context;
- raw tool logs.

## Proposed commands

```bash
grok handoff export [--format json|markdown|bundle]
grok handoff import <path>
grok handoff inspect <path>
```

Add `/handoff` equivalents in the TUI.

## Implementation plan

1. Define a stable, versioned JSON schema and a human-readable Markdown rendering.
2. Build export from structured session/workflow state, not only LLM summarization.
3. Use summarization only for narrative fields and label it as generated.
4. Add redaction and path/size limits.
5. Validate imports before creating a new session.
6. Show an import preview and let the user choose which sections to inject.
7. Record provenance so the new session can link back without depending on the original process.
8. Support importing from other agents when they can produce the schema.
9. Add deterministic tests using fixture bundles and migrations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exported bundle can start a fresh session with no access to the original session store.
- [ ] The default bundle is substantially smaller than the transcript and excludes unrelated history.
- [ ] Secrets and known sensitive fields are redacted.
- [ ] Import preview shows exactly what context will be injected.
- [ ] Unknown schema versions fail safely.
- [ ] Missing referenced files/commits are reported but do not corrupt the source.
- [ ] JSON and Markdown represent the same core data.

## Tests

- Round-trip export/import.
- Schema migration.
- Secret redaction.
- Oversized diff/attachment limits.
- Missing repository/file/commit.
- Import into a different cwd/model/provider.
- Malformed/untrusted bundle.
- Deterministic ordering for version control.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not call this “resume.”
- Do not inject the full transcript by default.
- Do not include credentials or hidden reasoning.
- Do not execute commands during import.

issues.title: [P2][startup] Add a composable bare startup profile
[P2][usage] Report usage per provider/model and distinguish unknown quota
[P1][maintenance] Reconcile the upstream mirror and certify fork invariants after sync
issues.body:
## Summary

At the refreshed audit point (2026-07-31), `providers` contains merge commit `eafa57c`, which integrates verified upstream `dd04f39`. The fork's `main` mirror still points at `a5727c5`, however, and the large upstream integration has no durable sync record proving that every provider/security invariant was rechecked.

The current code is no longer simply "five commits behind". The remaining work is to reconcile the documented branch contract and certify the already-integrated upstream delta rather than blindly merge it again.

## Evidence / affected code

- `origin/main`: `a5727c5` at the refreshed audit point.
- `upstream/main`: `dd04f397b1d02f2272b092555669dfba1f01bc85`.
- `providers`: merge commit `eafa57c43bfc1d0d8516ffceee5371c45759eb8f` includes that upstream target.
- Fork-specific hot spots overlap the upstream delta in sampler request construction, model catalog/config handling, pager model switching, session lifecycle, subagents, and custom-model documentation.

## Branch contract

- `main`: pristine, reviewable upstream mirror.
- `providers`: shipping multi-provider/local-model product branch.
- Fork-specific conflict resolution belongs on a uniquely named sync branch before landing on `providers`.

## Implementation plan

1. Verify the configured upstream remote by exact URL/repository identity and record the fetched SHA.
2. Reconcile `main` with the verified upstream target without adding fork-only commits.
3. Produce a durable sync record for the `dd04f39` integration, including the actual merge base, merge commit, and reviewed conflict/hotspot list.
4. Re-run and record all fork security invariants:
   - no first-party session credentials on external origins;
   - keyless auth scrubbing;
   - catalog ID/wire slug separation;
   - readiness fail-closed behavior;
   - subagent credential inheritance boundaries;
   - first-party metadata stripping.
5. Re-run the provider hot-path build, lint, and tests on the reconciled graph.
6. Update `FORK.md` and the sync process documentation so later syncs start from the same explicit branch contract.
7. If corrective code is required, land it through a focused PR to `providers`; do not hide it in mirror maintenance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `main` matches the recorded, verified upstream target and contains no fork-only commits.
- [ ] `providers` contains the upstream target plus all documented fork invariants.
- [ ] A sync record identifies the upstream SHA, merge base, merge commit, reviewed hot spots, and verification commands.
- [ ] Multi-provider CI and security regression tests pass at the reviewed commit.
- [ ] No conflict marker, temporary patch, or generated artifact remains.
- [ ] Custom-model docs match the effective configuration.
- [ ] Version/update behavior is intentionally reviewed.

## Validation

At minimum:

```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo check -p xai-grok-sampler -p xai-grok-shell -p xai-grok-pager
cargo test -p xai-grok-sampler
cargo test -p xai-grok-shell
cargo test -p xai-grok-pager
```

Also run the dedicated multi-provider mock integration suite once implemented.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not merge another upstream head merely to satisfy this issue; first certify the already-integrated target.
- Do not edit `main` to resolve fork-specific behavior.
- Do not assume upstream security behavior automatically satisfies fork boundaries.
- Do not use a date-only branch name that can collide on retry.

issues.title: [P1][CI] Add a complete multi-provider regression gate
[P1][CI] Add macOS and Windows provider smoke coverage
issues.body:
## Summary

The fork's CI currently runs on Ubuntu only, while the project documents macOS support and best-effort Windows builds. Multi-provider behavior depends on platform-specific environment handling, config paths, process execution, terminal behavior, TLS roots, and localhost networking.

Add focused cross-platform smoke coverage without duplicating the entire Linux suite.

## Scope

Matrix:

- Ubuntu (existing full gate);
- macOS latest supported runner;
- Windows latest supported runner.

Cross-platform smoke tests:

- compile relevant binaries/crates;
- parse custom-model TOML;
- resolve env-key credentials;
- anonymous loopback provider request;
- Bearer and `x-api-key` request construction;
- CLI model/doctor/inspect JSON;
- session creation and model selection without a real TUI;
- paths with spaces and non-ASCII characters;
- line endings and shell-independent test commands.

## Implementation plan

1. Extract platform-neutral mock-provider tests into Rust tests rather than shell scripts.
2. Add a small CI matrix for `xai-grok-sampler`, `xai-grok-shell`, and CLI/pager parse tests.
3. Use native path/temp-directory APIs.
4. Avoid Bash-only environment setup on Windows.
5. Cache Cargo artifacts safely by OS, Rust version, and lockfile hash.
6. Set explicit timeouts and upload redacted diagnostics.
7. Mark the matrix required once stable; do not leave Windows permanently `continue-on-error`.
8. Document any unsupported platform feature with a targeted skip and issue reference.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The same keyless/Bearer/`x-api-key` smoke tests pass on all matrix OSes.
- [ ] Paths with spaces/non-ASCII work.
- [ ] No platform job requires real credentials.
- [ ] Failures are reproducible locally with documented commands.
- [ ] Windows is not hidden behind unconditional `continue-on-error`.
- [ ] CI runtime/caching are reasonable.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not attempt full interactive terminal snapshots on every OS in this issue.
- Do not use platform-specific shell quoting in shared tests.
- Do not claim support beyond what the tested artifact provides.

issues.title: [P1][ops] Make upstream sync atomic, resumable, and repository-safe
[P1][docs] Replace upstream installer guidance with fork-specific instructions
issues.body:
## Summary

The default `providers` branch README still reads like the upstream project and points users at the official x.ai installer. Running that installer does not install this fork's multi-provider/local-model changes.

The README also retains an upstream contribution statement that can mislead users about whether this fork accepts issues or pull requests.

## Required documentation

Add a prominent fork banner that explains:

- this is an independent fork, not an official xAI distribution;
- `providers` is the shipping fork branch;
- `main` is the pristine upstream mirror;
- which multi-provider features are fork-specific;
- how to install/build the fork;
- how updates differ from upstream;
- supported platforms and tested status;
- where to report fork issues/contribute;
- security warning for third-party provider credentials.

## Implementation plan

1. Rewrite the README opening before any official installer command.
2. Move official upstream installation into a clearly labeled “Install upstream Grok Build” section or remove it from the fork's primary path.
3. Add fork install paths:
   - build from source;
   - verified fork release artifacts once available;
   - version verification showing fork commit/channel.
4. Link `FORK.md` and the custom-model guide.
5. Add a quick-start example for:
   - anonymous local provider;
   - external provider using an env var.
6. Replace the contribution policy with the fork's actual policy.
7. Explain branch targeting for PRs (`providers`, not `main`).
8. Include a migration note for users who previously ran the official installer.
9. Keep all commands executable and covered by docs validation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new reader cannot mistake the official installer for the fork installer.
- [ ] Fork/upstream identity and branch roles are explicit above the fold.
- [ ] Install/build commands produce a binary with identifiable fork version information.
- [ ] Provider examples use env vars and no literal secrets.
- [ ] Contribution/issue instructions match repository settings.
- [ ] Links and code blocks pass docs validation.

## Tests

- Link check.
- Execute build/version commands in CI.
- Parse every TOML example.
- Secret-pattern scan on examples.
- Verify referenced paths/files exist.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not imply endorsement or support by xAI.
- Do not publish an unverified binary URL.
- Do not remove upstream license/attribution.

issues.title: [P2][release] Add reproducible fork releases with checksums and provenance
issues.body:
## Summary

Users need a reliable way to install the fork without accidentally installing upstream. Add a fork-specific release pipeline with reproducible inputs, distinct version/channel identity, checksums, SBOM, and provenance.

## Versioning/channel requirements

- Never reuse or overwrite upstream tags/releases.
- Use a clearly fork-specific scheme, for example:
  - upstream version + fork revision;
  - `fork-vX.Y.Z.N`;
  - another documented monotonic format.
- `grok version --json` must identify:
  - upstream base/version;
  - fork version;
  - commit SHA;
  - release channel;
  - build target.

## Artifacts

At minimum for supported/tested targets:

- macOS arm64/x86_64 as appropriate;
- Linux x86_64 (and additional targets only when tested);
- Windows x86_64 once smoke coverage is required.

Publish:

- archives/binaries;
- SHA-256 checksums;
- CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM;
- signed provenance/attestation;
- release notes including upstream base and fork changes.

## Implementation plan

1. Define the release/version contract in `FORK.md`.
2. Add a tag-triggered workflow with pinned Actions.
3. Build from a clean checkout with the committed lockfile.
4. Run the required multi-provider/security gates before packaging.
5. Embed immutable version metadata.
6. Produce deterministic archives where practical (stable ordering/timestamps).
7. Generate checksums, SBOM, and artifact attestations.
8. Sign release metadata/artifacts using GitHub OIDC/attestation or a documented signing approach.
9. Publish to a fork-specific update channel; do not point fork binaries at the upstream auto-update channel.
10. Add install/verify commands to README.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fork and upstream versions are unambiguous in CLI and filenames.
- [ ] Every artifact has checksum, SBOM, and provenance.
- [ ] Release workflow cannot publish when required tests fail.
- [ ] Artifacts are built only from the tagged commit.
- [ ] Update behavior cannot silently replace the fork with upstream.
- [ ] Installation and verification commands are documented and tested.
- [ ] A dry-run workflow can validate packaging without publishing.

## Tests

- Workflow dry run on a test tag or manual dispatch.
- Verify embedded commit/version.
- Verify checksums and attestations.
- Install/unpack smoke test per target.
- Compare repeated builds for reproducibility where runner/toolchain permits.

## Dependencies

- Complete cross-platform smoke coverage.
- Complete multi-provider regression gate.
- Fork-specific README/version contract.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not publish artifacts from pull-request code with release credentials.
- Do not use floating third-party Actions.
- Do not call unsupported targets supported.

issues.title: [P2][security] Pin CI actions and add dependency/supply-chain checks
issues.body:
## Summary

CI currently references reusable Actions/toolchain setup by moving tags or version-like refs. The workspace also has a large dependency surface, including Git dependencies. Add explicit supply-chain controls appropriate for a security-sensitive CLI that handles credentials and executes tools.

## Scope

- Pin every third-party GitHub Action to a full commit SHA.
- Document the human-readable version in a comment.
- Automate reviewed pin updates.
- Audit Rust dependencies, licenses, sources, and advisories.
- Generate an SBOM for releases.
- Prevent accidental unpinned Git dependencies.

## Implementation plan

1. Replace floating Action refs with immutable SHAs.
2. Enable Dependabot or Renovate for:
   - GitHub Actions;
   - Cargo dependencies.
3. Add `cargo-deny` policy for:
   - advisories;
   - licenses;
   - bans/duplicates where justified;
   - sources (crates.io and explicitly approved Git repos).
4. Add `cargo-audit` or equivalent advisory checking if it provides complementary coverage.
5. Verify every Git dependency uses an immutable `rev`, not a branch/tag.
6. Add a lockfile consistency check.
7. Add secret scanning for fixtures/docs/log snapshots.
8. Generate an SBOM in the release pipeline.
9. Document exception handling with owner, reason, and expiry.
10. Use least-privilege workflow `permissions` blocks and prevent untrusted PR code from accessing release secrets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No third-party Action uses a floating tag.
- [ ] No Git dependency uses an unpinned branch/tag.
- [ ] Advisory/license/source policy runs on PRs.
- [ ] Exceptions are explicit and expiring.
- [ ] Workflow permissions are minimal.
- [ ] Secret-pattern scans do not expose matched secret content in logs.
- [ ] Release artifacts include an SBOM.

## Tests / verification

```bash
cargo deny check
cargo audit
cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1
```

Add a CI self-check that rejects non-SHA `uses:` references except approved local actions.

## Guardrails / non-goals

- Do not auto-merge dependency updates without tests/review.
- Do not fail on duplicate dependencies without evaluating build/runtime impact.
- Do not print suspected secrets into CI logs.
